videos.topic: Delhi iron pillar: why it has not rusted away (phosphorus, thin protective layer)
videos.title: Why Hasn't This 1,600-Year-Old Iron Pillar Rusted Away? 🇮🇳 #shorts #mystery #india
videos.format: Hindi audio hf_beta x1.0, English subtitles, 31.8 s, single story, bright look
videos.status: uploaded private, awaiting Rutvi to publish in Studio
sources: IUPAC Chemistry International, 'A New Fence Protects the Delhi Iron Pillar' reprint of M. Veazey, Materials Performance (2005): https://old.iupac.org/publications/ci/2005/2706/3_veazey.html (about 1,600 years old; Qutub Minar complex; about 7.3 m; it does rust but the passive rust is thin and protective; phosphorus crucial; slag with little lime left phosphorus in the iron)

R. Balasubramaniam, IIT Kanpur, 'New Insights on the Corrosion Resistant Delhi Iron Pillar' (2001): https://core.ac.uk/download/297714691.pdf (1,600-year-old; thin protective iron hydrogen phosphate hydrate layer; phosphorus; wetting and drying)

The Naked Scientists, 'A Rust-free Iron Pillar Yields its Secret at Last' (2002): https://www.thenakedscientists.com/articles/science-news/rust-free-iron-pillar-yields-its-secret-last (high phosphorus reacts with air and water to make a protective layer; limestone was not added)

Down To Earth, 'Iron mask' (2002): https://www.downtoearth.org.in/environment/iron-mask-15049 (thin protective layer; high phosphorus compared with modern iron; ancient iron made with charcoal, without limestone)
University of Oxford, Department of Chemistry, Corrosion: https://vrchemistry.chem.ox.ac.uk/potential/text/corro1.htm (ordinary iron oxide flakes away, exposing fresh metal)
EarthDate, 'Rust Results': https://www.earthdate.org/episodes/rust-results (rust forms with water and oxygen, flakes off and exposes new metal)
videos.notes: Third Friday Short, made on a manual re-run after Rutvi deleted the first two. Left out the phosphorus percentage, film thickness and weight (sources differ), and the Delhi-climate and mass theories. Fits her Nov 27 feedback: topic Indians already know, Hindi, no listicle.
